blocks.text: Cape Horn Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: Cape Horn is the established residential slope in south Coquitlam above the Cape Horn interchange, where Highway 1 (the Trans-Canada Highway), Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) and the Mary Hill Bypass (Highway 7B) meet at the Port Mann Bridge approach.
The City tracks the area as planning areas 15 and 16 in its development statistics, rather than as a named neighbourhood plan.
Cape Horn Avenue and Mariner Way are the residential roads connecting the slope to the interchange, with United Boulevard the light-industrial and commercial road below it.

Next to it: Maillardville and Coquitlam West to the west and north-west, Central Coquitlam up Mariner Way to the north, Port Coquitlam across the Coquitlam River and the Mary Hill Bypass to the east, and Surrey across the Port Mann Bridge to the south.

blocks.text: Cape Horn Houses: the housing stock

items.t: Houses here are freehold-led detached stock on a slope, with the City's own permit record for the area in the statistics year entirely in single-family, suite and carriage-house form, and no townhouse or apartment units created.

blocks.text: Cape Horn Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The slope is the rule, not the interchange, because a lot's rebuild depends on its grade, its creek edge and its access, not on how close it sits to Highway 1.

blocks.text: Cape Horn Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Mackin Park in Maillardville is the verified City park on the south-west side near Cape Horn, and the Poirier Sport and Leisure Complex area serves the same side of the city.

blocks.text: Cape Horn Houses: development and new projects

items.t: The plan-level item touching these houses is the Austin Heights and Maillardville side of the city, not a Cape Horn project: the Austin Heights Neighbourhood Plan, Schedule J-1, governs the centre to the west, with medium-density housing as a buffer to lower-density houses.

blocks.text: Cape Horn Houses: costs and taxes

items.t: The Cape Horn-specific point is slope drainage: the City's residential total includes a separate drainage rate, and a larger sloped lot with more hard surface is the kind of lot where that rate is worth reading.
The interchange is the point: Highway 1, Lougheed Highway and the Mary Hill Bypass meet below the slope, with the Port Mann Bridge crossing the Fraser River immediately east.
No SkyTrain station is inside Cape Horn itself, so transit from these houses is a bus connection first, not a station walk.

blocks.text: Cape Horn home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

18 houses sold in Cape Horn with a median price of $1,332,500 (the middle half sold between $1,107,500 and $1,384,000), taking a median of 22 days to sell at 97.0% of the last list price; 22% sold above list. They had a median $551 per square foot, a median year built of 1982 and a median lot of 7,333 square feet.

faq.q: How many houses are for sale in Cape Horn?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 14 houses listed in Cape Horn. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Cape Horn a buyers’ or sellers’ market for houses?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses in Cape Horn had a sales ratio of 14%, which the reports’ scale reads as a balanced market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many houses sold in Cape Horn from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 10 houses sold in Cape Horn over those 5 months, out of 273 in all of Coquitlam.

faq.q: Does this page include townhomes or duplexes in Cape Horn?
faq.a: No. The figures are for detached houses only. Condos and townhomes are counted on their own page.

faq.q: Which elementary school is actually in Cape Horn?
faq.a: Cape Horn Elementary, at 155 Finnigan Street, is the School District No. 43 (Coquitlam) elementary school inside this area, with phone 604-526-4428.

faq.q: Can I add a suite or carriage house to a Cape Horn house?
faq.a: The Cape Horn-specific limit is the lot itself: subdivision minimums of 650 square metres in R-1 and R-3 and 465 square metres in R-2, plus the creek, slope or pre-1945-house check, and a watercourse permit for creek-edge lots.

faq.q: Is Cape Horn in the Fraser floodplain?
faq.a: Not in the way a riverfront lot is. The City's floodplain mapping covers the Coquitlam, Fraser and Pitt river floodplains, while Cape Horn sits on the slope above the interchange lowlands; the water risk to check lot by lot is Cape Horn Creek and slope drainage, not a river dike.

faq.q: What did houses in Cape Horn sell for?
faq.a: 18 houses sold in Cape Horn between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $1,332,500.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Cape Horn?
faq.a: The median was 22 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.0% of the last list price (22% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
